conviction_note: Two arithmetic reads of Porch's own filings point to a beat and a raise: Q3 consensus of $133.4M Porch-owned revenue implies ~16% y/y growth against 23% in Q2 and 29% in Q1, and the FY guide implies H2 below the Q2 run-rate. Against that, the $345M H2 RWP management quoted needs +31% y/y against +17% in H1, and the stock is +42% since the last print and sits at the analysts' average target, the same setup in which the Q3 2025 beat sold off 33%. abs_move 20 (implied 18.7, median past reaction 21.9) and p_up 56 give +2.4. The findings sum to +2.5, so the two measures agree. The upside-paid skew and 14.5% short interest (much of it likely convert-hedge) argue against sizing the negatives larger.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $133.4M (range $129.5-138.0M, 6 analysts) and EPS $0.02, Walnut Invest (https://walnutinvest.com/stocks/prch/forecast, updated Oct 2026); Benzinga agrees at $133.2M / $0.02 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PRCH/earnings-forecasts). FY consensus $514.1M sits inside the company guide of $506-517M (Porch-owned segments, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001784535/000178453526000046/prch-20260729xexx991.htm), so consensus is on the Porch-owned (ex-Reciprocal) basis. Two agreeing sources, so the bar is sourced. Caveat: Benzinga's Q2 'estimate' was $122.6M against $131.8M Porch-owned / $140.9M consolidated, so the aggregators' basis has been loose.
positioning_check: Short interest 16,481,840 shares = 14.52% of shares outstanding, 9.32 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30 (down 4.9% from 17.33M / 12.9 DTC on 2026-09-15), per https://altindex.com/ticker/prch/short-interest. As a share of float it is higher (other sources show 19.8-21.8% of float). A large part is plausibly convert-arbitrage hedging: $134.0M 9% 2030 notes convert at $15.72, in the money at a $17.59 spot (~8.5M shares), and $333.3M 6.75% 2028 notes convert at $25.00 (~13.3M shares), per https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001784535/000178453526000046/prch-20260729xexx991.htm and the 2025 notes release. Skew: 25d put minus call is -6.29 vol points, so upside is paid. Put/call OI 0.69. Event-implied move 18.66%. The stock is +42% since the close before the Q2 print ($12.36 on 2026-07-29 to $17.59) and -5.4% from its 52-week high; the average analyst target is ~$18.42 (MarketBeat 2026-08-02).

findings.finding: Q3 consensus of $133.4M Porch-owned revenue (Walnut, 6 analysts; Benzinga $133.2M) implies only ~16% y/y growth on Q3 2025's $115.1M Porch Shareholder Interest revenue, against 23% y/y in Q2 2026 ($131.8M) and 29% in Q1 2026 ($109.4M). Last year Q3 Porch-owned revenue was 7% above Q2. Holding Q2's 23% growth gives ~$141.6M, about 6% above the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been bought on 6 of the last 7 prints: Q2 2026 +16.0% (revenue $140.9M vs $122.6M estimate), Q1 2026 +17.9%, Q4 2025 +12.5%. The exception is Q3 2025: revenue $115.1M against $111.2M and EBITDA $20.6M against $16.7M (both beats), net loss -$10.9M, stock -33.4% (https://www.itiger.com/news/1103112742).
findings.why_not_priced: The bar itself shows sell-side has not extrapolated H1 growth: $133.4M is only 1.2% above Q2's $131.8M. If the street had priced Q2's trend, the consensus would sit near $140M and the estimate range ($129.5-138.0M) would not lie entirely below a 23%-growth outcome. The 42% run-up and upside skew show a beat is partly expected anyway, so this is sized well below the implied move.
findings.independence: The consensus comes from https://walnutinvest.com/stocks/prch/forecast and Benzinga. Q3 2025 base: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251105000353/en/Porch-Group-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results. Q1 2026: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001784535/000178453526000028/prch-20260428xexx991.htm. Shares the Q2 exhibit with the guidance finding.

findings.finding: The FY2026 guide implies a conservative H2 that the company has already raised past twice. Guide: Porch-owned revenue $506-517M, adj. EBITDA $119-125M, raised from $495-507M / $103-109M in April and $475-490M / $98-105M in February. H1 actuals were revenue $241.2M ($109.4M + $131.8M) and EBITDA $58.8M ($19.7M + $39.1M). That leaves H2 at $265-276M revenue, about Q2 x2, and $60-66M EBITDA, below Q2 x2 = $78M. In 2025, Q3 EBITDA ($20.6M) was above Q2's (~$15.6M).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide was raised at the Q1 and Q2 2026 prints, with +17.9% and +16.0% reactions, and at Q3 2025 (gross profit and EBITDA raised), which fell 33.4% after a large run.
findings.why_not_priced: FY revenue consensus of $514.1M sits inside the guide, below the top, so the street models H2 at the guide and not at the H1 run-rate. A priced raise would show consensus above $517M and EBITDA above $125M. The shares' 42% rise since July is consistent with a raise being partly expected, so the size is kept below a third of the implied move.
findings.independence: Q1 exhibit for the prior guides: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001784535/000178453526000028/prch-20260428xexx991.htm. On the Q2 call (https://www.webull.com/news/15364638842037248) management said it was 'ahead of schedule' on medium-term targets. Shares the Q2 exhibit with the reported-quarter finding, but rests on a different line: the full-year range against the run-rate.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call the CFO said the company expects $345M of Reciprocal Written Premium in H2 to reach the $600M FY target. H2 2025 RWP was $263.2M (Q3 $137.5M + Q4 $125.7M), so $345M needs +31% y/y. H1 2026 grew +17% ($254.3M) and Q2 only +16%, while RWP per policy fell 16% and competitors priced aggressively from May. Q3 is the first test. Policies would need to rise from 58.7k toward ~65k at roughly $2,600 per policy to put Q3 near $170M; a Q3 of ~$155-165M would leave Q4 needing +45% and put the $600M target in doubt.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RWP decelerated in Q2 (+16%) and the stock still rose 16% on the revenue beat and raise, so this line has been looked through while EBITDA beats. It has not yet been tested against an explicit H2 RWP number the company put on record.
findings.why_not_priced: Previews and the aggregators carry revenue and EPS but no RWP estimate. The H2 $345M figure comes from the call, not the release, and the +31% arithmetic against H2 2025 needs Q3 and Q4 2025 RWP from two older releases. If priced, the July-October rally would have stalled on RWP and the skew would not pay upside. Net of the rest of the company: Insurance Services revenue grew 38% in Q2 on 16% RWP growth, and the revenue/EBITDA guide does not depend on hitting $600M, so this is sized below the beat findings.
findings.independence: FY2025 RWP $480.9M and Q4 $125.7M: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260211650821/en/Porch-Group-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-2025-Results. Q3 2025 RWP $137.5M: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251105000353/en/Porch-Group-Reports-Third-Quarter-2025-Results. Competitive pricing in May and the target's dependence on pricing and agent incentives: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/porch-group-q2-earnings-call-highlights (summary of the same call, so not independent of the source).

findings.finding: The Reciprocal's Q3 should print strong capital. Q3 2026 was a benign catastrophe quarter: Texas hail reports were down ~70% in H1 2026 against the 2023-25 average (Moody's), global insured cat losses for 9M 2026 were 29% below the 10-year average, the Atlantic season was quiet through Q3, and the first hurricane landfall was 9 Oct in Florida. The Reciprocal is Texas-heavy. Q2's gross loss ratio was 38% with Q2 the 'highest weather' quarter. The Reciprocal also holds ~16.2M PRCH shares, up from ~$12.6 (late July) to $16.66 at 30 Sept, which lifts the 'surplus plus non-admitted assets' headline by roughly $60-70M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Management leads with Reciprocal surplus: it cited $412M of surplus plus non-admitted assets at Q3 2025, which fell 33% on other lines. No clean history of a surplus surprise moving the stock on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: benign weather is public, and Porch-owned EBITDA is largely insulated from Reciprocal losses since the legacy captive contract ended. The value is in the surplus headline and growth capacity before the Allied Trust closing, which is said to be surplus-neutral. This is macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by Porch for Q3, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Proxy. Q3 cat data from Gallagher Re via https://www.claimsjournal.com/news/national/2026/10/21/340831.htm (2026-10-21). Reciprocal's 16.2M PRCH holding is in the Q2 exhibit, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001784535/000178453526000046/prch-20260729xexx991.htm. Prices from Yahoo daily bars.

findings.finding: On 13 Oct 2026 Porch agreed to buy Allied Trust's Texas carrier, MGA and captive reinsurer for $200M. Porch-owned HoldCo pays $95M ($75M cash + up to $20M stock) for the MGA and captive. Management guides ~$200M of added RWP and ~$25M of adj. EBITDA (ex-Reciprocal) at under 4x. Closing is not before 1 Jan 2027. The call is the first chance for a 2027 framework that includes it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On announcement the stock went $17.69 to $17.22 (13 Oct) and $16.44 (14 Oct, -7.1% over two days), then recovered to $17.57 on 15 Oct and $18.59 on 21 Oct. The deal was digested at roughly flat.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: public for two weeks and the stock round-tripped. What is unpriced is any 2027 outlook combining organic growth with the $25M of deal EBITDA (FY26 guide midpoint $122M). Financing question answered: the $75M cash buys a ~4x-EBITDA earnings stream, not distress, so the sign is non-negative.
findings.independence: Terms and the $25M EBITDA / $200M RWP figures: https://www.reinsurancene.ws/porch-group-to-acquire-allied-trusts-insurance-carrier-and-mga/ (reporting the company's own release, same underlying document).

findings.finding: Expectations are high into the print. PRCH is +42% from the $12.36 close before the Q2 print to $17.59, -5% from its 52-week high, and near the ~$18.42 average analyst target. Q3 2025 was the same setup, with the stock up 68% and 22% on the two prior prints: a revenue and EBITDA beat with a raised guide fell 33.4% when the market focused on the net loss.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 -33.4% on a beat after a large run. Q2 2026 +16.0% from a much lower base ($12.36, after a weak spring).
findings.why_not_priced: The options market does not price this: skew is -6.3 vol points (upside paid) and put/call OI is 0.69, so the crowd is leaning long into the print. Short interest is 14.5% of shares outstanding with 9.3 days to cover, which can drive a squeeze. Much of it is likely convert-hedge, but it is still a reason to keep this negative small. Management has guided to positive FY net income, so last year's specific trigger (a net loss) is less likely.

outside_window.finding: The 9.00% convertible notes due 2030 ($134.0M, conversion price $15.72) become callable from 20 Nov 2026 if PRCH trades at or above 120% of conversion (~$18.86) on 20 of 30 trading days. A forced conversion would retire high-coupon debt. Any call is after the exit window, though the call could flag intent.
Allied Trust closing (Texas DOI approval required, not before 1 Jan 2027, outside date 1 Apr 2027).

baseline_tension: The two beat/raise findings agree with the upside-paid skew and the six-of-seven positive reaction history. The RWP and expectations negatives cut against both, which is why they are sized small and p_up sits at only 56 after a 42% run into a print that resembles the Q3 2025 sell-off setup.
lessons_applied: Rule 7 (positioning): the expectations/run-up negative shrunk from -1.5 to -1.0 because it sits against an upside-paid skew (-6.3 vol pts) and 14.5% short interest with 9.3 days to cover
Rule 7 + rule 9: the RWP-target negative shrunk from -2.5 to -2.0, net of Insurance Services revenue and EBITDA guidance that do not depend on the $600M target, and against the skew
Rule 5 (proxy): the weather/Reciprocal-capital finding trimmed from +1.0 to +0.8 because Porch has not confirmed Q3 transmission
Rule 6: bar checked against two agreeing sources ($133.2M Benzinga, $133.4M Walnut), so no cap applied; both beat findings left standing
